items.title: Digital responsibility, skills and environmental awareness for digital sustainability
items.abstract_excerpt: This study investigates how digital competencies and environmental awareness interact to shape eco-friendly digital practices, contributing to the field of digital sustainability. Drawing on a representative sample of adult internet users in the United Arab Emirates (N = 1016), it explores (H1) whether individual responsibility predicts environmentally conscious digital practices; (H2) whether environmental awareness moderates the effect of…

items.title: Guidance over guidelines? Unpacking the uses and concerns of generative AI in communication science
items.abstract_excerpt: The rapid adoption of generative Artificial Intelligence (genAI) tools has transformed research practices across communication science. As genAI tools (and most notetably large language models), made the generation of text, images, and other media content extremely easy, they can potentially disrupt the way science is conducted. Yet, their integration into academic workflows has outpaced systematic understanding of how, when, and why…

items.title: Afterword: the waning power of the fix
items.abstract_excerpt: This commentary offers some reflections on the ‘power of the fix' in cybersecurity and its wider implications for technological democracy. I begin with a discussion of the discrepancy between the discourse of solutionism and everyday practices of securing IT systems (Elgaard Jensen et al, 2026). Whereas the former posits that problems are neat and can be solved by means of technology, the latter must confront what Röhle (2021) has called the…

items.title: Predicting Irritation Disclosures in Romantic Relationships: Testing and Extending the Revelation Risk Model
items.abstract_excerpt: Feelings of irritation often emerge in romantic relationships. However, the theoretical mechanisms predicting whether individuals disclose these feelings to their romantic partner remain limited and largely reliant on examining indicators of future behavior rather than actual future behavior. Using a two-month, longitudinal survey design involving 448 participants, the current study tested the Revelation Risk Model (RRM) as a mechanism for…

items.title: Democratic Media Performance and Democratization: A Global Longitudinal Perspective
items.abstract_excerpt: Media that effectively perform their democratic functions are widely considered a key driver of democratization, yet longitudinal evidence on their impact remains limited. This study analyzed global annual time-series data on democratic media performance and democratization from 1946 to 2018. ARIMA models indicated a covariation between annual increases in democratic media performance and gains in democratization worldwide, measured by…

items.title: Political Actors and Their Media Practices: Analyzing the Role of Media Participation in Democratic Backsliding and Resilience
items.abstract_excerpt: This paper draws together insights from political science and political communication to advance a new understanding of the role of media in democratic backsliding and resilience. The central argument is that all political actors may also be media actors, although they may do so anonymously or use false identities. Thus, mass participation in media enables mass participation in political change, with better and worse democratic outcomes. As…

items.title: How social media produces “Cheap Europe”: Digital Balkanism and the politics of creator mobility
items.abstract_excerpt: Digital platforms increasingly mediate how socioeconomic unevenness becomes visible, often recoding structural inequality as consumable value. This article introduces the concept of digital Balkanism to explain how platformed travel content reworks long-standing intra-European hierarchies. Drawing on a critical discourse analysis of 108 English-language YouTube videos about Bulgaria, we identify five recurring frames: cheapness-as-freedom…

items.title: The “Netflix Look”: Moving image aesthetics as data under platform logic
items.abstract_excerpt: This article examines Netflix’s industrial model through the framework of platform logic, arguing that the data-centric approach it adopts in the production of moving images alters the creative process. The result is a conceptual shift from shooting a film to capturing an image. Bridging platform studies and film theory, I build on David Bordwell’s poetics of cinema, which conceives the production process as a negotiation between institutional…

items.title: From platform outrage to institutional consequence: Convergent hybrid media accountability in Morocco
items.abstract_excerpt: This article develops the concept of convergent hybrid media accountability (CHMA) to explain how informal digital criticism is translated into institutional consequence in Morocco’s hybrid media environment. Moving beyond the view of accountability as an internal professional virtue, the article argues that where formal bodies are fragile or distrusted, citizens use platformed publics to initiate scrutiny from outside media institutions…

items.title: When Past Hurt Meets Present Care: How Family History Shapes Adult Caregivers’ Communal Coping With Siblings in Their Caregiving for Parents With Health Challenges
items.abstract_excerpt: This sequential, explanatory mixed-methods study explores how adult caregivers’ perceived family functioning and unresolved hurt toward siblings from childhood are associated with their present-day communal coping (CC) with their siblings and caregiving outcomes. Study 1 tested a hypothesized moderated mediation model using survey data ( N = 776). The results indicate greater childhood family functioning (consistent with hypotheses) and…

items.title: Does Office Type Determine Gendered Campaign Messages?
items.abstract_excerpt: This study examines how candidates’ gender shapes campaign messaging across different branches and levels of political office. Prior research offers mixed evidence on whether women are more likely than men to emphasize communal traits and women-related policies, often because gender effects are examined without fully accounting for institutional context. We address this inconsistency by foregrounding the role of electoral institutions. Building…

items.title: The Democratic Cost of Pursuing Virality: A Study into Parliamentary Communications
items.abstract_excerpt: The transformation of parliamentarians into media producers has heightened concerns about emerging forms of political communication. This mixed-methods paper examines the strategies they employ to enhance their digital presence. Based on in-depth interviews, it shows that Brazilian parliamentarians believe that social media penalize them for posting about congressional matters, reporting that content about legislative work and constituency…

items.title: Stephen Duncombe, Æffect: The Affect and Effect of Artistic Activism
items.abstract_excerpt: As with the philosophers and critics, among artistic activists there is no one universally agreed-upon notion of what artistic activism does.Depending on whom you speak to, artistic activism makes ideas accessible or it surprises and confuses, it reveals realities or it imagines new ones, it creates conversations or facilitates participation, it circumvents barriers to acceptance or creates spaces and places for creativity, it generates affect…

items.title: News Media, Narrative Authority, and the Global Ordering of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract_excerpt: This article examines how mainstream Western news media structure global hierarchies of technological legitimacy in coverage of artificial intelligence (AI). Although AI circulates worldwide, its public meaning is shaped within a restricted geopolitical and linguistic sphere. Conceptualizing news discourse as a narrative infrastructure that organizes visibility, authority, and technological futurity, we analyze 43,027 English-language newspaper…

items.title: One-Dimensional Algorithm: Rereading Marcuse’s Critical Theory Through Platform Culture
items.abstract_excerpt: This article rereads Herbert Marcuse’s critical theory through algorithmic curation on commercial social media platforms, pursuing a dialectical argument in two directions: first, that platform capitalism structurally reproduces Marcuse’s diagnoses of false needs, incorporation, and one-dimensional thought; second, that platform dynamics exceed his framework—in its passive-subject assumptions, its vagueness about resistance, and its inability…

items.title: “ In a way, I want TikTok to tell me what I want. . . ” Users’ experience of TikTok as a televisual algorithmic flow
items.abstract_excerpt: This article revisits Williams’s concept of flow, Firth’s notion of algorithmic flow, and Picone et al.’s concept of Small Acts of Engagement (SAOE) to examine how users experience TikTok’s algorithmic flow. SAOE are understood as low-effort, everyday acts through which users negotiate their identities and shape their digital consumption. While SAOE have been a valuable lens for understanding user agency on earlier social media platforms, we…

items.title: Are they virtue-signalling or sincere? The impact of perceived motives on the effectiveness of online collective action
items.abstract_excerpt: Social media is an important tool used by supporters of modern social movements to persuade others to participate. However, people who engage in online collective action often face speculation about their motives and may be perceived as acting for self-serving reasons. How do these perceptions impact the effectiveness of collective action? In three experiments ( N = 916), participants viewed posts (Study 1) or an immersive social media feed…

items.title: Cross-platformization: How U.S. right-leaning media curate their posts on Twitter and Truth Social
items.abstract_excerpt: This study examines how seven right-leaning media organizations utilize cross-platformization strategies to reach audiences across multiple platforms; in this case, Twitter and Truth Social. Focusing on both content volume and story packaging, we collect right-leaning media organizations’ social media posts and content from the 2022 U.S. midterm election.
